summary: This bill amends federal criminal law to replace discretionary sentencing with a 30-year mandatory minimum prison term for aggravated sexual abuse and sexual abuse.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends federal criminal sentencing statutes to impose mandatory minimum prison terms for sexual abuse offenses. It contains no provisions related to federal budgets, appropriations, or expenditures of any kind.
The bill addresses only criminal penalties under Title 18 and has no tax-related content whatsoever.
No provisions touch on healthcare delivery, insurance, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
The legislation does not mention firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration, border, or visa provisions appear in the bill.
The bill is silent on reproductive rights or abortion access.
No defense spending, military policy, or national security appropriations are involved.
The bill contains nothing related to environmental regulation or climate policy.
No welfare, entitlement, or social services programs are addressed.
The legislation does not reference schools, education funding, or school choice.
No drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance provisions exist.

The bill directly amends 18 U.S.C. §§ 2241 and 2242 to replace discretionary sentencing language with a mandatory minimum of 30 years to life for aggravated sexual abuse and sexual abuse. This constitutes a clear policy choice for substantially tougher, determinate sentencing rather than rehabilitation-focused or discretionary approaches.
No trade, tariff, or globalization measures are present.
The bill has no fiscal or deficit implications.
No provisions address LGBTQ legal protections or related civil rights.
Foreign assistance is not mentioned.
The bill does not touch on voting rights, election administration, or voter ID.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance provisions appear.
Labor law and union issues are absent.
The bill does not engage religious exemptions or anti-discrimination balances.
